translationRepairs: He then expelled Zhang Qiu from Jingyuan, Yang Shouzhong from Yangzhou, and Man Cun from Fengzhou, seized their territories, and petitioned to install his sons and brothers as governors, which the court was powerless to prevent.

He then expelled Zhang Qiu from Jingyuan, Yang Shouzhong from Yang Prefecture, and Man Cun from Fengzhou, seized their territories, and petitioned to install his sons and brothers as governors, which the court was powerless to prevent.
s0011 names 洋州, the Hanzhong command, not 揚州; English Yangzhou normally denotes the Jiangnan prefecture, so Yang Prefecture is the needed disambiguation.

In the seventh month of that year, Taiyuan's army reached Hezhong; Jipeng together with the palace eunuch Jing Xuan's son Jisheng forced the imperial carriage to go to Fengxiang; Emperor Zhaozong said: "Taiyuan's army has not yet arrived; the imperial carriage must not be moved lightly; I together with the princes will hold fast within the inner palace; you are to pacify the capital; if Taiyuan truly arrives, I can control them by strategy."

In the seventh month of that year, Taiyuan's army reached Hezhong; Jipeng together with the palace eunuch Jing Xuan's son Jisheng pressed the imperial carriage to go to Fengxiang; Emperor Zhaozong said: "Taiyuan's army has not yet arrived; the imperial carriage must not be moved lightly; I together with the princes will hold fast within the inner palace; you are to pacify the capital; if Taiyuan truly arrives, I can control them by strategy."
迫 marks coercion, but Zhaozong's immediate refusal and the later riot show the carriage did not go to Fengxiang in this sentence; forced ... to go overstates the outcome.

Yet in commanding troops he observed no discipline at all; at mealtimes he would go to the kitchens and often sit on the ground; even those who held the keys were addressed as Acting Grand Guardian — a far cry from the martial renown of Zhou Yafu and Feng Yi.

Yet in commanding troops he observed no discipline at all; at mealtimes he would go to the kitchens and often sit on the ground; even those who held the keys inside and outside were addressed as Minister of Works and Grand Guardian — a far cry from the martial renown of Zhou Yafu and Feng Yi.
內外持管鑰者 is omitted, and 司空太保 is the pair Sikong and Taibao, not the single title Acting Grand Guardian.

Maozhen soon received an imperial ordinance promoting him to Grand Preceptor of the First Rank, acting Grand Commandant, concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi army.

Maozhen soon, by delegated imperial authority, conferred on him the titles of opening an office with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Commandant, concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.
承制加 makes Maozhen the granter, and 彰義軍 follows Congyan's Jingzhou posting, so Maozhen is not the promotee; the proposal still mistranslates 開府儀同三司 as Grand Preceptor of the First Rank.

Maozhen soon received an imperial ordinance adding the titles of Grand Preceptor with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Commandant, and concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.

Maozhen soon by delegated authority added to him the titles of opening an office with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies, acting Grand Commandant, and concurrent Palace Attendant, commander of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign army, and military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.
承制加 is delegated conferral on Congyan, not Maozhen receiving an ordinance; the proposal restores 承制 but still leaves the beneficiary unnamed and keeps Grand Preceptor for 開府儀同三司.
At the end of Tang he was a capital garrison commander of Fengxiang; Maozhen memorialized him as military commissioner of Fu Prefecture; he rose in office to concurrent Palace Attendant.
At the end of Tang he was a garrison commander of Fengxiang; Maozhen memorialized him as military commissioner of Fu Prefecture; he rose in office to concurrent Palace Attendant.
鳳翔都將 is a Fengxiang garrison commander; 都 is the unit prefix, not the capital.

When the Liang founder besieged Fengxiang, Maoxun camped at Qishan; the founder baited him with a weak force and sent Kong Qian with elite troops to seize Fuzhou and capture his whole family; Maoxun then submitted to Liang, took the name Zhou Yi, and was made campaigning marshal at headquarters.

When the Liang founder besieged Fengxiang, Maoxun camped at Qishan; the founder baited him with a weak force and sent Kong Qian with elite troops to seize Fuzhou and capture his whole family; Maoxun then submitted to Liang, took the name Zhou Yi, and was appointed campaign adjutant of the Marshal's headquarters.
元帥府行軍司馬 is the campaign adjutant of the marshal's headquarters, not a campaigning marshal; the proposed parenthetical gloss is accurate but awkward in idiomatic English.

Soon he was made senior general of the Golden Crow Guard and assisted Wang Zan at Jingdian; when Zan posted him at the western camp, Zhuangzong attacked and defeated him, and he was demoted to senior general of the Left Guard.

Soon he was made senior general of the Jinwu Guard and assisted Wang Zan at Jingdian; when Zan posted him at the western camp, Zhuangzong attacked and defeated him, and he was demoted to senior general of the Left Guard.
金吾上將軍 is the Jinwu Guard; Golden Crow confuses 金吾 with 金烏.
Zhu was then appointed Grand Preceptor of the First Rank.
Zhu was then appointed to the rank of opening an office with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies.
開府儀同三司 is one prestige rank, ceremonial equality with the Three Excellencies, not Grand Preceptor (太師); copying Grand Preceptor from the literal still invents that office.
In the summer of the fourth year of Tiancheng Zhu died, and the court appointed his younger brother Cheng acting commissioner of the Shuofang army.
In the summer of the fourth year of Tiancheng, Zhu died, and the court appointed his younger brother Cheng acting commissioner of the Shuofang army.
The Chinese pauses after 天成四年夏 before 洙卒; without the comma, Tiancheng Zhu can be read as one name.

Soon the Prince of Jin sent Zhou Dewei with fifty thousand troops from Bin and Feng to attack Xiazhou; Renfu held out for over a month until Liang reinforcements arrived and Dewei withdrew; the founder was pleased and specially promoted him to acting Grand Guardian and Tongping Zhangshi.

Soon the Martial Emperor of Later Tang sent Zhou Dewei with fifty thousand troops from Bin and Feng to attack Xiazhou; Renfu held out for over a month until Liang reinforcements arrived and Dewei withdrew; the founder was pleased and specially promoted him to acting Grand Guardian and Tongping Zhangshi.
The actor is 後唐武皇, the Martial Emperor of Later Tang; Prince of Jin is not in this sentence.
Li Yichao has already been removed and appointed acting commissioner for observation of Yan Prefecture; he is to be compelled to proceed to his post at once.
Li Yichao has already been appointed acting commissioner for observation of Yan Prefecture; he is to be compelled to proceed to his post at once.
已除 is the appointment verb 除, not removal; removed and appointed reverses the office action.
